findings.title: Keep replies awaiting publication recovery immutable during reassociation
findings.evidence: owner_publication.py:74–78 updates an existing generated draft's commits and body without checking pending actions, unlike owner.py:89–93. For general feedback, a successfully posted reply is a separate timeline item, so refreshing does not change the source fingerprint checked at owner_publication.py:68–69. After a lost response and an amended exact commit, reassociation can rewrite the ambiguous draft. recover() then passes the old receipt to finish() at lines 149–153, and lines 165–168 mark the rewritten current reply Published. A bounded in-memory reproduction using production refresh, association, receipt validation, and recovery confirmed that the Published body referenced the replacement SHA while its receipt contained only the old wording. The broader inline-thread scenario was rejected because the posted reply changes the thread fingerprint.
findings.body_md: A generated timeline reply can have an `ambiguous` submission after GitHub accepted it but the response was lost. If the author amends/pushes an exact replacement commit and runs association before recovery, this branch rewrites the draft's commits and body. The original general-feedback fingerprint remains unchanged because the reply is a separate timeline comment. Recovery subsequently finds the old marker and marks the rewritten draft Published using the old receipt, reporting wording and a commit link that were never sent. Apply the pending-action immutability check before reassociation changes the reply, or recover an immutable submitted version separately from the editable draft.

findings.title: Restore acknowledged general feedback to the Attention group
findings.evidence: owner.py:78–80 sets restored triage to attention but computes visibility only from unread state, change_requested, or an unresolved thread. An acknowledged, deferred timeline comment therefore returns triage='attention' and attention=False; a bounded execution of production mutate() confirmed this. owner_state.py:218–220 repeats the calculation during refresh. emacs/magit-auto-review-owner.el:171–175 filters the Attention group on attention, leaving the restored item in History.
findings.body_md: After acknowledging an ordinary timeline comment, defer it and invoke Restore. Restore sets `triage='attention'`, but `unread` is false and the item has neither an outstanding change-request verdict nor an unresolved thread, so this calculation leaves `attention=False`. The comment stays in History, and refresh preserves that result. Make explicit restoration return acknowledged general feedback to Attention, with matching behavior in the refresh calculation.

findings.title: Preserve dependency references when replacing replanned tasks
findings.evidence: At lib/pr_review/owner_fixes.py:221–225, changed feedback requeues its completed task. Lines 249–261 retain other completed tasks and replace the changed task with a newly prefixed ID, without updating retained depends_on references. Adoption at lines 203–211 reactivates those retained tasks, and line 271 indexes the missing prerequisite. An in-memory execution reproduced a ready replanned batch containing p1-dependent -> p1-base alongside p2-base, followed by KeyError('p1-base') on adopt=True.
findings.body_md: If completed task B depends on A and only A's feedback changes, replanning replaces A with a new prefixed task but retains B's dependency on A's removed ID. The batch can become ready, yet later adopting manual changes reactivates B and crashes at the dependency lookup. Preserve a valid combined dependency graph by remapping references or replanning affected dependents; cover the replan-then-adopt recovery path.

findings.title: Keep uncertain replies immutable during commit reassociation
findings.evidence: lib/pr_review/owner.py:89–93 protects pending replies during ordinary mutations, but owner_publication.associate at lines 75–78 checks only whether an existing reply is Published before replacing commits/body. For general feedback, a successful timeline response is a separate item and does not change the original source fingerprint. A narrowed in-memory reproduction reassociated an ambiguous commit-A reply to B, then recovered A's valid timeline receipt. owner_publication.finish at lines 165–168 marked the commit-B body Published with the commit-A receipt.
findings.body_md: A generated timeline reply can have an ambiguous submission after GitHub accepts it but its response is lost. Reassociating that batch to a new commit currently rewrites the same unpublished reply, despite its pending action. Recovery then marks the rewritten body and commit Published using the receipt for the original post, corrupting the published record and making it immutable. Reject or defer association updates for replies referenced by submitting/ambiguous actions until recovery completes.

findings.title: Recheck the PR open state before every reply POST
findings.evidence: owner_publication.prepare rejects non-OPEN PRs at lib/pr_review/owner_publication.py:124–125. However, the per-reply refresh at lines 182–186 validates only head identity and reply blockers before reaching the POST at lines 196–197. A focused reproduction used real prepare/publish functions: preview and re-prepare saw OPEN, the next refresh saw CLOSED with the same head, and publication still reached one mocked POST.
findings.body_md: If the PR closes or merges after publication's second prepare, the per-reply refresh observes that state but execution still sends the reply when the head is unchanged. This bypasses the open-PR requirement already enforced during preparation and also affects the remainder of a partially published batch. Check metadata.state == OPEN after every pre-send refresh, before recording/sending another action, while retaining confirmed receipts.

findings.title: Keep uncertain replies immutable during reassociation
findings.evidence: owner_publication.py:75–78 rewrites unpublished replies without checking submitting/ambiguous actions. recover()/finish() at lines 140–168 attaches the original action receipt to that mutable draft. A focused reproduction recovered a Published draft claiming commit new while the receipt contained Fixed in old. Ordinary mutation already rejects uncertain replies in owner.py:91–95.
findings.body_md:
Source: Codex. Confidence: High.

If a generated timeline reply succeeds remotely but its response is lost, reassociating an amended commit rewrites its pending body and commits. Recovery then marks that rewritten draft Published using the original receipt, misrepresenting what was posted. Freeze replies referenced by submitting or ambiguous actions until recovery and retain the exact submitted payload as history.

findings.title: Preserve verified history when resume fails before execution
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:247 can fail preflight before new inference; lines 286–289 nevertheless overwrite ready with paused. owner_publication.py:27–32 accepts only ready batches. The reproduction confirmed ready becoming paused with an unchanged final_tree and no model calls.
findings.body_md:
Source: Codex. Confidence: High.

An authentication or discovery failure while resuming an unchanged ready batch removes its eligibility for commit association. Committing and pushing the previously verified tree then leaves association skipping the batch and resume rejecting changed HEAD. Preserve the accepted verification record until changed inputs or execution invalidate it; record preflight failure separately.

Source: Codex. Confidence: High.

findings.title: Prevent published owner replies from invalidating remaining replies
findings.evidence: owner_state.py:204–208 uses fingerprint(item), including owner comments, for content dependency changes. Source: Claude. Confidence: High.

Exclude known self-publication receipts from dependency invalidation, or safely advance expected context while continuing to detect incoming changes.

Source: Claude. Rejection confidence: High.

findings.title: Bind interrupted-task skips to the interrupted task
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:197–200 accepts any nonempty skip list. Source: Claude. Confidence: High.

After a failed writer attempt whose resulting tree was captured, skipping an unrelated task satisfies the interrupted-task gate and replays the interrupted fixer. Require every interrupted writer task to be explicitly adopted or included in the skip selection. The existing worktree comparison protects uncheckpointed edits but does not validate which task the user authorized skipping.

findings.title: Preserve the implementation stage for queued tasks during adoption

Source: Claude. Confidence: High.

Adopting partial changes for an interrupted batch moves unrelated queued tasks directly to review. Those tasks lose their initial implementation stage; any first fix requested by review consumes their repair allowance. Reviews still prevent automatic unverified acceptance, but valid remaining work can pause prematurely. Preserve queued tasks and distinguish them from work requiring reverification.

findings.title: Scope Git integrity checks to relevant shared configuration

Source: Claude. Confidence: High.

findings.title: Make network owner operations cancellable from Emacs
findings.evidence: emacs/magit-auto-review-owner.el:278–287 starts asynchronous operations and learns cancellation IDs only from started events; lines 450–452 require that ID. owner.py:41–60 dispatches refresh/prepare/publish/recover without operation(), unlike owner_fixes.py:171. The focused dispatch reproduction confirmed refresh emits no started event. The close guard at owner.el:67–71 also refuses buffer termination while the process runs.
findings.body_md:
Source: New. Confidence: High from code tracing and backend reproduction; Emacs execution was not run.

A slow GitHub refresh, preparation, publication, or recovery cannot be cancelled with K because these commands never register the operation ID K requires. The buffer close guard also refuses termination and directs the user to K. Register long owner operations with shared cancellation, or provide a safe process fallback that preserves uncertain publication intent and releases locks.

findings.title: Reject dirty initialized submodules before accepting checkpoints
findings.evidence: Source: Codex #1. owner_git.py:105-107 stages a superproject tree; dirty contents beneath an unchanged submodule gitlink are not represented. admin() at lines 81-93 does not inspect submodule worktrees. owner_providers.py:148-149 consequently accepts such read-only-role edits and omits fixer edits from final_tree. Scenario: an initialized submodule file changes without a submodule HEAD change. Code-traced; no runtime submodule fixture was run.
findings.body_md: An initialized submodule can have modified files while retaining the same gitlink SHA. These checkpoints and the admin digest then remain unchanged, allowing planner/reviewer writes to pass and omitting fixer changes from saved diffs. Reject dirty initialized submodules, including nested ones, or capture and validate their contents recursively. Source: Codex. Confidence: high from code tracing.

findings.title: Exclude removed and explicitly skipped feedback from replanning
findings.evidence: Sources: Codex #2 and Claude #1. owner_state.py:222-231 retains missing items and marks dependent batches stale; items() at 156-161 rejects them. owner_fixes.py:249-253 excludes only completed items, and line 263 requests all original items again. A production-function mock reproduced invalid_target with one missing item, replan=True, and its task explicitly skipped. Skip processing actually precedes the stale check, contrary to Claude's ordering claim. Manual commit/reconciliation remains possible.
findings.body_md: When selected feedback is deleted, refresh retains it as missing. Replanning still includes it even after its task is explicitly skipped, so context construction raises invalid_target before independent tasks continue; the full-batch fingerprint update has the same problem. Preserve skips/removal history and build planning/fingerprint selections from available active items. Source: Both. Confidence: high; reproduced with in-memory mocks.

findings.title: Resolve repository identity before reading the remembered toolkit
findings.evidence: Sources: Codex #3 and Claude #5. Forge opening at magit-auto-review.el:490 omits repository. The added lookup at 508 passes that omission to owner_state.toolkit(); lines 90-101 leave identity unset with distinct fork/upstream remotes. An in-memory preference-store reproduction saved Owner under an explicit identity and received Reviewer from the unscoped lookup.

It silently opens Reviewer. Resolve or select the repository before preference lookup and pass the same identity to the selected toolkit. Source: Both. Confidence: high; preference mismatch reproduced.

findings.title: Owner replies invalidate verification fingerprints
findings.evidence: Source: Claude #2. owner_state.py:110-114 distinguishes complete conversation fingerprints from viewer-filtered notifications; lines 206-231 invalidate assessments on content changes. owner_publication.py:68-69 refuses automatic drafts from changed verification context. The mock confirmed that an owner reply changes the full fingerprint while leaving the notification unchanged. The documented changed-discussion policy supports this conservative invalidation; the observed behavior alone does not demonstrate the claimed defect.

Refusing to reuse an assessment after that context changes is consistent with the documented policy. Excluding every owner-authored message could also miss changes in agreed scope. Source: Claude. Confidence: high in observed behavior and the policy distinction.

findings.title: Restrict bulk selection to explicit feedback groups
findings.evidence: Source: Claude #3. magit-auto-review-owner.el:88-104 selects all matching descendants within the current section without validating group type. The root at 154 encloses attention and history feedback, and line 235 defaults point to point-min. Therefore root selection includes actionable deferred/handled items. Full Emacs verification failed because Magit was missing; an isolated harness failed before assertion. Classification rests on source tracing.
findings.body_md: At the initial root heading, this descendant scan selects feedback across the entire buffer, including hidden Deferred/History items. Pressing f can start fixes for those items, and triage commands can affect them all. Allow bulk selection only on explicit eligible groups, otherwise raise the existing selection error. Source: Claude. Confidence: high from code tracing; full Magit behavior was not runtime verified.

findings.title: Owner opening requires explicit repository selection with ambiguous remotes
findings.evidence: Source: Claude #4. owner_state.py:42-55 deliberately rejects distinct remote identities before Repository.resolve(). The API and implementation promise no network access on owner-open, while --repo, repository selection, and PR URLs provide disambiguation. A mock confirmed invalid_request without calling the resolver. The reviewer's gh repo view fallback would violate the owner's offline-open contract.
findings.body_md: Rejected: refusing ambiguous local repository identity is consistent with offline owner opening and explicit repository selection. The supplied scenario has supported --repo/URL/list-selection alternatives. An unconditional network fallback is not an appropriate correction. This does not resolve the separate preference-key mismatch in F3. Source: Claude.

findings.title: Avoid copying ignored-path inventories into repeated prompts
findings.evidence: Source: Claude #6. owner_git.py:110-111 places the full ignored-file inventory in each checkpoint. owner_fixes.py:81-85 includes complete completed-task records in provider context, including before/after checkpoints; owner_providers.py:132 serializes that context. A small reproduction observed an ignored filename twice in one completed task's prompt data. Large inventories consequently amplify payloads, but no actual latency or model-limit failure was measured, and transient checkpoints do not necessarily enlarge persisted session state.
findings.body_md: Completed-task context includes before/after checkpoints with full ignored-file lists, so large dependency/build inventories are repeatedly serialized into state and downstream model prompts. Store inventories once by reference or summarize them, and omit them from provider context. Source: Claude. Confidence: high for duplication; performance and token-limit consequences remain unmeasured.

findings.title: Publishing performs repeated complete refreshes
findings.evidence: Source: Claude #7. owner_publication.py:175-186 performs preparation and a refresh/fetch per reply. The repeated calls are real, but they revalidate account, discussion, permissions, and head immediately before writes. No measured rate-limit, timeout, or latency failure was supplied or reproduced. A head-only replacement would omit required discussion checks.
findings.body_md: Rejected as a demonstrated defect. Per-send freshness checks intentionally protect external writes. The extra initial refresh may be optimizable, but call count alone does not establish a failure, and checking only the head would weaken existing safeguards. Source: Claude.

findings.title: Saved push mapping may diverge from the refreshed target
findings.evidence: Source: Claude #8. owner_git.py:70-74 configures branch tracking only when configured_target is absent. A mock with an old configured branch and a new push_target confirmed no configuration writes. However, no supported live PR-head repository/branch transition or resulting wrong Git/Magit push was established. Existing tests explicitly preserve later manual configuration; push behavior can also refuse a mismatched destination.
findings.body_md: Conditional risk: if GitHub reports a different head repository/branch after initial setup, the displayed target can differ from the saved branch mapping. The one-time guard is confirmed, but a reachable end-to-end wrong-push scenario is unverified. Prefer surfacing the mismatch for explicit reconciliation while preserving human overrides. Source: Claude. Confidence: high in conditional code behavior, low in the claimed push failure.

findings.title: Require skips to cover interrupted tasks before continuing
findings.evidence: Source: Claude #9. owner_fixes.py:197-200 lets any nonempty skip list bypass interruption handling; lines 212-217 validate only that listed tasks exist. With t1 fixing, t2 skipped, no adoption, and a current tree equal to the saved checkpoint, the production execute() mock launched fix/review for t1. run_task() at 91-97 resets its before checkpoint. Earlier attempt artifacts remain, narrowing the original record-loss claim.
findings.body_md: A nonempty skip list bypasses the interruption gate even when it names only an unrelated task. If the current tree matches the saved checkpoint, the interrupted fixer is restarted without adoption and its task-level before checkpoint is reset. Validate skips first and require each interrupted task to be skipped or explicitly adopted. Source: Claude. Confidence: high; restart reproduced with mocks.

findings.title: Fix and resume repeat provider preflight and freshness checks
findings.evidence: Source: Claude #10. owner_fixes.py:247 invokes preflight on each operation; owner_providers.py:31-64 performs metadata/capability/authentication checks. The README explicitly documents fresh metadata and live probes for every fix operation. check_fresh() and its task-loop calls protect against discussion changes between tasks. No accidental call outside an explicitly requested fix operation or demonstrated failure was established.
findings.body_md: Rejected as a defect: repeated preflight is explicitly documented behavior, and task freshness checks guard against intervening discussion changes. Session caching would change that policy and requires its own invalidation design; the supplied cost/latency concern was not demonstrated as a failure. Source: Claude.

findings.title: Recheck PR state before every reply send
findings.evidence: Source: New. owner_publication.py:124-125 checks OPEN only during preparation. The send loop at 182-186 refreshes metadata but checks only head equality; it then creates an action and posts at 197. A focused mock changed metadata to CLOSED during the loop refresh while preserving the head, and production publish() still issued one send and recorded a published receipt. No live GitHub request was made.
findings.body_md: If the PR closes after preparation or between replies without changing its head, the next refresh reports CLOSED but this loop still sends the reply. Recheck the refreshed PR state before each action/POST, preserving confirmed receipts and stopping the remainder when it is no longer OPEN. Source: New. Confidence: high; the client write attempt was reproduced with mocks.

findings.title: Reject dirty submodules before accepting checkpoints
findings.evidence: owner_git.py:105-107 snapshots a superproject tree; admin() at 78-93 does not inspect submodule state. owner_providers.py:145-149 accepts unchanged tree/admin values. Editing files inside an initialized submodule without changing its HEAD leaves the gitlink unchanged, so provider-introduced edits evade verification and are absent from final_tree. Initial clean() only catches preexisting dirt. Established by code tracing; no real-submodule runtime check ran.

These checkpoints omit that content, and the administrative digest does not inspect nested repositories. Planner/reviewer writes can therefore pass integrity checks, and fixer changes disappear from saved diffs and `final_tree`. Recursively reject dirty submodules before accepting checkpoints, or explicitly capture and verify their contents. The initial clean-worktree check does not catch edits introduced during a provider invocation.

findings.title: Preserve skips and exclude unavailable feedback when replanning
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:249-253 excludes only completed items from replanning; line 261 replaces other tasks, and line 263 requires all original feedback again. owner_state.py:156-161 rejects missing items retained by refresh at 222-231. A focused execution reproduced invalid_target for deleted skipped feedback. A separate completed execution with extant feedback and skip=['a'] showed the planner receiving ['a','b'] and execution running both.

Confidence: high.** When selected feedback disappears during a paused batch, `replan` still includes it and raises `invalid_target`, even if its task was explicitly skipped. The same selection/replacement logic also revives skipped feedback that still exists. Preserve explicit skips and their dependency effects, exclude unavailable/skipped items from executable planning, and update fingerprints without requiring deleted items at line 263. This expands the original deleted-feedback finding with a reproduced skip/replan interaction.

findings.title: Resolve the repository before looking up its toolkit
findings.evidence: magit-auto-review.el:479-488 opens Forge PRs without passing a repository; 508-511 queries toolkit before resolving it. owner_state.py:90-107 infers identity only for a single unique remote and otherwise reads a key containing None. An in-memory call to the actual toolkit function with upstream/fork remotes returned Owner for the explicit repository and Reviewer for the unscoped request.

Opening a PR through Forge passes no repository here, so the backend reads a different preference key and defaults to Reviewer. Resolve and pass the Forge repository identity before this lookup. Single-remote inference works; the explicitly scoped PR-list entry point also remains a workaround.

findings.title: Preserve accepted verification when resume fails before execution
findings.evidence: Source: Codex A comment 2. owner_fixes.py:247 performs preflight after selecting an existing ready batch; lines 286-289 overwrite its status on any exception. owner_publication.py:27-33 permits only ready batches. The changed-HEAD preservation branch at owner_fixes.py:186-191 applies only while status remains ready. findings.body_md: Resuming an unchanged ready batch while discovery/authentication is unavailable changes its status to Paused even though no plan/fix/review invocation or content change invalidated the accepted verification. If the user then commits and pushes that verified tree, automatic association skips the batch, explicit association rejects it, and resume fails because HEAD changed. Preserve the accepted verification independently of the latest execution failure, or retain readiness when the failure occurred before anything invalidated the verified result.

findings.title: Recheck open-PR state before every reply submission
findings.evidence: Source: Codex A comment 3. owner_publication.py:124-125 rejects closed PRs during prepare, but lines 182-186 refresh metadata and check only head and reply blockers before sending. A two-reply in-memory reproduction observed refresh states OPEN, OPEN, OPEN, CLOSED with unchanged head and still recorded two successful timeline sends, both marked Published. Confidence: High.
findings.body_md: If the PR closes or merges after preparation or between replies, this refresh observes its new state but publication continues when HEAD is unchanged. Remaining timeline comments are sent and marked Published despite the open-PR restriction in `prepare()`. Check the refreshed PR state before recording each submission intent and sending; retain already confirmed receipts and leave the remaining drafts available for inspection.

findings.title: Pause on clarification before automatic repair
findings.evidence: Source: Codex B comment 1. owner_fixes.py:52-65 accepts clarification outcomes independently of complete; successful() at lines 68-69 rejects them. The task repair predicate at lines 113-118 and combined predicate at lines 148-152 nevertheless allow complete=true plus blockers without excluding clarify. Schema-valid focused reproductions produced review -> fix at both checkpoints for a clarification requiring a human decision. Confidence: High.
findings.body_md: A review with `complete=true`, blocking findings, and a `clarify` outcome still launches the writable fixer through this condition. The equivalent combined-review condition has the same omission. Consequently automation can make further source edits while a required human decision remains unresolved. Exclude clarification outcomes from both automatic-repair predicates and persist the paused/needs-attention state before returning.

findings.title: Staleness fingerprint includes owner's own comments; multi-reply publication aborts and batches go stale
findings.evidence: owner_state.py:205 `content = fingerprint(item)` is not viewer-filtered; lines 206-207 add the key to `changed`, which unstages unpublished replies (226-228) and marks batches stale (229-231). owner_publication.py:181-186 refreshes before each reply, and blockers() (108-111) raises on a fingerprint mismatch. Reproduced: two staged replies on thread:T1 → publish posts 1, raises stale_discussion; statuses ['published','unstaged'].
findings.body_md: `fingerprint(item)` (owner_state.py:205) includes the viewer's own comments, so every reply the owner publishes marks the thread changed. In `publish`, the second staged reply on the same thread is unstaged and `blockers()` raises `stale_discussion` partway through a confirmed publication. Batches containing the item also become `discussion_stale`. Use the viewer-filtered `notification` fingerprint for invalidation and staleness.

findings.title: invoke() sets batch checkpoint to post-run tree before checking returncode/result
findings.evidence: owner_providers.py:147 `batch["checkpoint"] = after` precedes the integrity check (148), the returncode check (150) and result validation (152-164). On a failed or timed-out fix, the partial tree becomes the checkpoint; on resume, owner_fixes.py:201 (`snapshot != checkpoint`) does not fire, so with --skip the partial edits are silently carried forward. Code trace; the harness mocks invoke.
findings.body_md: A fix attempt that fails or times out after editing files has its partial tree adopted as `batch["checkpoint"]` (owner_providers.py:147) before any success checks. This bypasses the `worktree_changed` explicit-adopt gate on resume. With `--skip`, unreviewed partial edits flow into later tasks and `final_tree`, and they are hidden from the re-run task's `task_diff`. Assign the checkpoint only after all checks pass.

findings.title: Interrupted-task gate accepts any non-empty --skip
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:199 `if not request.get("adopt") and not request.get("skip")` only checks that skip is truthy; the interrupted task (status fixing/repairing) stays unskipped and run_task (88-94) re-launches a fix on the current checkpoint. Combined with F2, this replays on top of partial edits.
findings.body_md: `--skip p1-other` satisfies the interrupted-task guard even when a different task (`p1-t1`) is the one in `fixing`. That task is then re-run without adopt or skip, contradicting the documented 'do not blindly replay a partially applied task' rule. Require every `fixing`/`repairing` task to be in `skip`, or require `adopt`.

findings.title: Adopt converts never-run queued tasks to review-only
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:207-211 sets every task not skipped/blocked (including queued) to status 'reviewing' with implementation 'Manually adopted changes'; run_task (91) skips the fix for 'reviewing' tasks. A no_change, non-blocking review marks them complete without implementation.
findings.body_md: When adopting after an interrupt, queued tasks that never ran are moved to `reviewing` with the summary "Manually adopted changes", so the fix role is never invoked for them. They either 'complete' with nothing implemented or use up their single repair. Only move tasks that were started (or that have `before`) to review, and keep `queued` tasks queued.

findings.title: admin() hashes entire shared .git/config, causing false integrity failures
findings.evidence: owner_git.py:84 hashes session.repo.common/'config'. Any user config write (push -u, remote add) or a later configure_push write changes the identity → integrity_failed in invoke (owner_providers.py:95) and execute (owner_fixes.py:194). The PR's own test test_fork_missing_and_ambiguous_remotes_are_explicit must pass adopt=True after adding remotes.
findings.body_md: Hashing the entire shared `.git/config` into the admin identity flags unrelated user config writes as provider tampering, forcing adopt-and-reverify. Hash only the keys that matter (`branch.<owner-branch>.*`, `core.hooksPath`, `include*`, `core.fsmonitor`).

findings.title: Toolkit choice / owner-open break with multiple remotes and nil repository
findings.evidence: owner_state.py:93-101 stores the toolkit under digest([common, None]) when there are several remotes; pulls.py looks up the explicit repository. emacs/magit-auto-review.el:490 calls --open-pr with nil repository from Forge; :508 queries toolkit with nil. owner_state.py:50-51 raises 'Choose a repository' for nil identity with >1 remote.
findings.body_md: In fork checkouts (origin plus upstream), the Forge entry passes a nil repository. `toolkit()` then reads and writes a `None`-keyed record that differs from the one the PR list uses, and `owner-open` raises 'Choose a repository'. Resolve the repository the same way as the reviewer path before the toolkit lookup.

findings.title: Resume mutations applied before settings/staleness validation
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:203-218 applies adopt/skip/requeue before the settings_changed (226-227) and stale_discussion (219-220) raises; the except handler (286-290) saves. The persisted state equals the user's explicit request, and the next resume re-validates the snapshot, admin identity and settings, so impact is limited.
findings.body_md: `execute()` mutates the batch for adopt/skip/replan and then may raise `settings_changed`/`stale_discussion`, and the handler persists the half-applied request. Impact is low because the persisted change is what the user asked for and safety checks repeat on the next resume. Still, validate before mutating.

findings.title: Full discussion refresh before every task and every published reply
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:161-166 check_fresh → refresh before each task and twice after the loop (275, 283); owner_publication.py:182 refresh per reply. refresh (owner_state.py:170-187) does gh pr view + REST PR + /user + paginated lists + GraphQL. Modified: context snapshots are content-addressed (line 237), so new files appear only on change, and the double PR read is a deliberate consistency check.
findings.body_md: Every task and every published reply triggers a full PR plus discussion download (several REST pages and GraphQL calls), which adds latency and rate-limit pressure on busy PRs. Consider a cheap head-SHA check between tasks and one full refresh at the boundaries.

findings.title: Owner preflight duplicates and drifts from reviewer auth-probe validation; re-runs paid probes
findings.evidence: owner_providers.py:59-60 accepts falsy is_error, while reviews.py:165 requires `is_error is False`; the Codex check (56-57) does not reject 'error'/'turn.failed' events as reviews.py:166 does. preflight is called on every execute (owner_fixes.py:247).
findings.body_md: `preflight()` re-implements the reviewer's live auth-probe validation with weaker checks (`not is_error` vs `is False`; no Codex `error`/`turn.failed` rejection) and launches paid probes on every `owner-fix` call. Share one helper and cache a successful preflight per batch or settings.

findings.title: batch_diff and task_diff duplicated when before == baseline
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:81-85 always computes both; the plan (253) and final_review (137) pass batch['baseline'] as before, making them byte-identical.
findings.body_md: The plan and final-review prompts contain the full combined diff twice because `task_diff` equals `batch_diff` when `before == baseline`. Omit `task_diff` in that case.

findings.title: Missing feedback re-marked changed on every refresh; batches cannot recover
findings.evidence: owner_state.py:222-225 re-adds every previously missing item to `changed` each refresh (they persist in state['feedback']). Batches stay discussion_stale; replan calls session.items on batch items (owner_fixes.py:263 / context at 253), which raises invalid_target for missing keys (owner_state.py:160-161). Reproduced: after dropping thread:T2, stale stays True across refreshes and `owner-fix --replan` → invalid_target.
findings.body_md: Once any feedback item is deleted, every later refresh puts it back in `changed`, so its batches are `discussion_stale` forever. Resume needs `--replan`, and replan fails in `session.items` with 'Feedback is no longer available'. The batch can never finish, and a new batch requires a clean worktree. Flag only the transition into missing, and let replan skip or withdraw missing items.

findings.title: associate aborts for all ready batches when any associated item is missing
findings.evidence: owner_publication.py:67 `item = session.items(state, [key])[0]` raises invalid_target for a missing key inside the loop over all batches/associations. Reproduced: ready batch, commit pushed, associate OK (2 replies); drop one item → associate raises 'Feedback is no longer available; refresh first.'
findings.body_md: A single deleted feedback item makes every `owner-associate` call fail, even for unrelated ready batches, and refreshing cannot clear it. Skip and report associations whose source is missing instead of raising.

findings.title: execute() error handler demotes a 'ready' batch to 'paused'
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:286-290 sets status 'paused' on any exception once batch is bound; only the HEAD-changed path (189-191) is protected. CLI resume defaults to the latest batch (owner_cli.py:67). Reproduced: ready batch + new comment → resume → stale_discussion → status 'paused' → associate --batch rejects 'Choose a batch with a successful combined review'.
findings.body_md: Resuming a `ready` batch (CLI `resume` defaults to the latest batch) that hits any error, such as a new comment, a settings change or a network failure, rewrites its status to `paused`. `associate` then refuses it, and a successful resume re-runs the paid final review. Preserve `ready`/`final_tree` when no new work started, or refuse to resume ready batches without an explicit reverify.

findings.title: Checkpoints store full ignored-file list, propagated into state and model prompts
findings.evidence: owner_git.py:110-111 lists all ignored files into every checkpoint; grep shows 'ignored' is never read. Task before/after checkpoints are included in context()['completed_tasks'] (owner_fixes.py:85) and json-dumped into every prompt (owner_providers.py:132).
findings.body_md: Every checkpoint records `ls-files --others --ignored`, which is unused, and it propagates into session.json, protocol views and (through `completed_tasks`) every plan, fix and review prompt. After a fix model installs dependencies or builds, this can be tens of thousands of paths. Drop the field and send trimmed task summaries.

findings.title: Checkpoint rehashes the entire worktree each call
findings.evidence: owner_git.py:105-106 runs `read-tree HEAD` into a fresh temp index (no stat cache), then `add -A`, so git must hash every file; invoke takes two checkpoints per provider call. Magnitude not measured.
findings.body_md: Each checkpoint builds a stat-less temp index, so `git add -A` re-hashes the whole worktree, at least twice per provider call. Seed the temp index from a copy of the worktree's real index to reuse the stat data.

findings.title: Require skipping the interrupted task before resuming
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:197–200 accepts any nonempty skip list; lines 267–280 subsequently run the still-fixing task. Skipping unrelated task B therefore restarts interrupted task A without adoption.
findings.body_md: A nonempty `skip` list bypasses the interruption guard even when it does not include the interrupted task. Require each interrupted task to be explicitly skipped, or require adoption before resuming it. Source: Codex. Confidence: high.

findings.title: Leave unstarted tasks queued when adopting partial work
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:207–211 marks all non-skipped, non-blocked tasks reviewing, including queued tasks. run_task at lines 95–106 then bypasses their fix invocation; a nonblocking no_change review can lead to ready status.
findings.body_md: Adopting an interrupted early task also changes never-started tasks to `reviewing`, so their planned fixes can be omitted. Reverify affected tasks while retaining queued tasks for execution. Source: Codex. Confidence: high.

findings.title: Flag an obsolete configured push target
findings.evidence: owner_state.py:228–233 refreshes push_target; owner_git.py:69–74 does not update or flag an existing configured_target. A push using the saved branch mapping can target the previous repository or branch.
findings.body_md: When the PR head destination changes, the displayed target changes but the existing Git push mapping remains. Detect the mismatch and require explicit reconciliation, preserving deliberate user configuration. Source: Codex. Confidence: high for the stale mapping; push behavior depends on Git settings.

findings.title: Do not let missing feedback block other associations
findings.evidence: owner_publication.py:61–68 looks up every pushed saved association; owner_state.py:158–164 rejects missing items. A deleted previously associated item aborts processing of other items in the batch.
findings.body_md: A deleted historical feedback item makes association of remaining valid items fail. Preserve the historical association, but skip or flag the unavailable destination and continue processing the others. Source: Claude. Confidence: high.

findings.title: Avoid invalidating verified work and staged replies on the owner's own comments
findings.evidence: owner_state.py:204–209 uses fingerprint(item) including viewer comments. owner_publication.py:67–69 silently skips a mismatched verified item; lines 181–186 refresh before each reply, so posting one of two replies to a thread can invalidate the second.
findings.body_md: The owner's own reply changes the full discussion fingerprint. This can suppress a fixed-in draft after verification or interrupt a prepared multi-reply publication after the first reply. Distinguish known owner-authored changes or safely rebase remaining confirmed replies. Source: Claude. Confidence: high from code tracing; live propagation was not tested.

findings.title: Permit replanning around deleted feedback
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:249–263 sends original missing keys to context/session.items and later rebuilds fingerprints from all batch items. owner_state.py:158–164 rejects those keys, including when their task was skipped.
findings.body_md: A deleted selected item prevents replanning the rest of a batch because missing items are still required in planner context and fingerprint rebuilding. Retain it as history and provide an explicit exclusion path for active work. Source: Claude. Confidence: high.

findings.title: Provider command restrictions may not prevent remote pushes
findings.evidence: owner_providers.py:75–83 supplies command-pattern denials, and owner_git.py:78–94 fingerprints local administrative state rather than remote branches. Whether git -C or git -c variants bypass the installed Claude permission matcher and have network access was not tested.
findings.body_md: The local integrity check cannot detect a remote push, so the safety of the cited command variants depends on provider permission matching and network restrictions. Verify those behaviors and enforce the no-push boundary independently if they permit the commands. Source: Claude. Confidence: insufficient to establish the claimed bypass.

findings.title: Toolkit selection without a repository can be stored under a null identity
findings.evidence: owner_state.py:94–105 writes a null-identity key when multiple remote identities exist; pulls.py:62–74 subsequently reads a repository-specific key. The standard PR-list frontend prompts for a repository first at magit-auto-review-pulls.el:89–92, limiting the reported scenario.
findings.body_md: When toolkit selection is invoked without repository context in a multi-remote checkout, the choice is stored under a key that repository-specific lookup does not read. Require a repository choice or define a consistent fallback. Source: Claude. Confidence: high for backend behavior; ordinary frontend reachability is limited.

findings.title: Repeated refreshes may increase API usage
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:161–166 refreshes between tasks and around final review, and owner_publication.py:181–186 refreshes before each submission. No rate-limit failure or latency measurement was supplied, and these checks protect freshness.
findings.body_md: Repeated network reads are present, but the report does not establish a user-impacting performance defect or an equivalent safe reduction. Source: Claude. Confidence: high in the observed calls; impact unverified.

findings.title: Validate the final provider authentication result
findings.evidence: owner_providers.py:55–61 accepts any matching success event, while reviews.py:165–166 checks the last Claude result and rejects Codex error and turn.failed events. A zero-exit stream with success followed by failure can pass the owner probe.
findings.body_md: Owner preflight can accept an earlier success even if later events indicate failure. Apply the existing reviewer's final-result and error-event validation. Source: Claude. Confidence: high for the validation gap; occurrence of such provider streams is unverified.

findings.title: Refresh the owner view when reopening an existing buffer
findings.evidence: magit-auto-review-owner.el:264–271 obtains a fresh view but accepts it only inside the new-mode branch. If another process updates the session, reopening retains the old revision until explicit reload.
findings.body_md: Reopening an existing owner buffer discards the freshly returned view, leaving stale display and revision. Accept the returned view on reopen so subsequent actions use current state. Source: Claude. Confidence: high.

findings.title: Duplicated combined-review repair policy
findings.evidence: owner_fixes.py:113–123 and 148–156 have separate repair handling, but owner_providers.py:136–167 records attempts and results. The reported difference does not demonstrate an incorrect outcome.
findings.body_md: The two repair paths duplicate policy, but the cited difference in report storage does not establish a functional bug. Source: Claude. Confidence: high for the code distinction; no demonstrated failure.

findings.title: Require adoption after a failed combined repair
findings.evidence: owner_providers.py:145–151 advances batch.checkpoint before checking a failed process. During final_review at owner_fixes.py:148–152 all tasks can already be complete; execute's exception handler pauses the batch, and its resume guard at lines 197–202 does not identify the failed combined repair when the snapshot matches the advanced checkpoint.
findings.body_md: If a combined-review repair edits files and then fails after checkpointing, a plain resume can proceed to combined review without the explicit adoption required for partial work. Persist the combined repair's interrupted state and require an explicit recovery decision. Source: New. Confidence: high for the traced failure path.

With `replan: true`, line 263 of owner_fixes.py (and `context()`/`final_review`) calls `session.items(state, batch['items'])`, which raises invalid_target ('Feedback is no longer available'). The owner composes and publishes a manual reply on thread A (its comments change, so `fingerprint` changes; `notification`, which excludes the viewer, does not). The owner then commits and pushes and runs associate: `item['fingerprint'] != batch['verified_fingerprints'][A]` hits `continue`, so no fixed-in draft is created and no error is shown. Opening the owner buffer and pressing `f` starts a fix batch for every actionable item, including ones already handled or deferred. Pressing `h`, `k`, `i` or `V` likewise changes triage for every feedback item instead of raising 'Choose an item or its group'.

   Failure scenario: In a fork checkout with origin and upstream remotes, `pr-review owner 123` or opening a PR from Forge via `magit-auto-review` (which passes no repository) fails with 'Choose a repository from this checkout's remotes'.    Failure scenario: In a multi-remote checkout the user picks Owner in the PR list, which saves it under key github.com/o/r. Opening a PR via `magit-auto-review` from Forge calls `--open-pr` without a repository, reads the None key, gets 'reviewer' and opens the reviewer buffer instead of the owner toolkit.

   Failure scenario: In a repo with node_modules or build output, `ls-files --others --ignored` lists more than 100k files. Each checkpoint (before/after for every invoke, resume, diff --current) adds that list several times, so session.json grows to tens of MB. Every save and Emacs refresh slows down, and `context()` puts the lists into the planner/fixer/reviewer prompt, which can exceed model limits. Use `--directory` or store only a hash.

7. `lib/pr_review/owner_publication.py:182`: `publish()` calls `prepare()`, which does a full refresh and fetch, then does another full refresh and `fetch_head` for each reply, starting with the first one right after prepare.

   Failure scenario: Publishing N staged replies runs N+1 full refreshes. Each one makes about six GitHub calls (gh pr view, pulls API, user, three paginated comment endpoints, GraphQL thread pages) plus a git fetch. Publishing 10 replies makes about 70 or more API calls and waits on them in sequence, which risks rate limits. The first iteration could reuse the prepare snapshot, and later ones could just check the head.

8. `lib/pr_review/owner_git.py:70`: `configure_push` writes branch remote/merge/pushRemote only once (it is guarded by `configured_target`), so the tracking config is never updated after the PR head repository or branch changes.

   Failure scenario: The PR author renames the head branch, or GitHub reports a different head repository. `refresh` updates `push_target`, but `branch.pr-owner/N.merge` still points to the old branch. Pushing from Magit in the owner worktree then sends the fixes to the old or wrong destination, while the buffer shows the new push target.

9. `lib/pr_review/owner_fixes.py:199`: The interrupted-task gate is bypassed by any non-empty `skip` list, even one that names an unrelated task, so the interrupted fixing or repairing task is silently restarted without the required adopt.

   Failure scenario: Task t1 is interrupted mid-fix (status 'fixing'). The user resumes with `--skip p1-t3`, which is unrelated. The check `not adopt and not skip` passes, t1 still has status 'fixing', and `run_task` runs a fresh fix with `before` reset to the current checkpoint, losing the record of the interrupted attempt instead of asking for inspection.

10. `lib/pr_review/owner_fixes.py:247`: Every `owner-fix` or resume runs `models.preflight`, which runs `--help` and a live authentication model probe for each provider. On top of that, `check_fresh` does a full GitHub refresh before every task.

    Failure scenario: Resuming a batch after a trust prompt or a pause, or a batch with many tasks, makes repeated live model probes (extra cost and delay up to `auth_timeout` each) and one full discussion refetch per task. Cache the preflight per settings for the session, and check freshness only at the head and fingerprint level.
